name: Selenite
spiritual: Said to cleanse other crystals and spaces
physical: Kept near the bed for restful sleep
Crystal healers link it to a feeling of lightness and flexibility
summary: Selenite is a soft, pearly gypsum named for the Greek moon goddess, used as the classic cleansing stone for peace, stillness and clearing crystals.
intro: Selenite is the glowing white wand on the shelf of nearly every crystal shop. It is a transparent to milky variety of gypsum that grows in long, flat-sided blades with a satiny, pearly shine and fine lengthwise ridges. Pieces range from small palm wands to the colossal beams of Mexico's Naica Cave, which grew up to 11 meters long. It is very soft, only 2 on the Mohs scale, and a fingernail can scratch it. People are drawn to selenite for its stillness: lamps, towers and plates made from it give a soft, glowing, moonlike light.
history: The name comes from Selene, the Greek goddess of the moon, a reference to the soft, moon-pale glow of the crystals. Since antiquity selenite sheets were cut thin and used as windows before glass was common, notably in Roman buildings and in parts of Spain and Mexico. The fibrous variety called satin spar was carved into beads and ornaments. Gypsum itself is used to make plaster of Paris and drywall. Selenite's reputation as a cleansing stone is a modern crystal-healing tradition, built on its clear, light look.
meaning: Crystal healers regard selenite as a stone of light and cleansing. It is said to clear stagnant energy from rooms and from other crystals, which is why plates and wands are used to recharge collections. It is linked to the crown chakra and soul star and is associated with calm, stillness and connection with higher guidance. Emotionally, it is said to ease agitation and bring perspective during anxious times. Practitioners place it around beds and entryways to promote peace and a feeling of protection. Some link it to a flexible, spacious feeling in the body and to restful sleep. It is considered a gentle but powerful stone for meditation, and many keep one in any space where they want quiet.
howToUse: Lay a selenite plate or bowl under your crystals overnight to cleanse them. Pass a wand slowly over the body or around a room while breathing out stress. Place a tower near the bed for peaceful sleep, or set a lamp in a corner for a soft glow. Sit with a wand held upright at the crown for meditation. Place four small pieces at the corners of a room or window sill for a protective feeling, and keep them dry.
care: Selenite is very soft and dissolves in water, so never wash or soak it. Wipe with a dry cloth and avoid humid places like bathrooms. Cleanse it with sound, breath or by placing it in moonlight, though selenite is traditionally considered self-cleansing. Avoid heat and keep it away from hard stones that could scratch it. Store wrapped in cloth, and handle wands gently since they can snap.
identify: Genuine selenite is soft enough to scratch with a fingernail and feels slightly waxy or silky. It is translucent with fine striations and a pearly sheen. Fakes include clear glass, calcite or resin; calcite is harder and fizzes in vinegar. Some selenite is dyed or color-coated for lamps. Satin spar is fibrous and shows a cat's-eye shimmer, while true selenite crystals are flat and transparent.

faq.q: Why is selenite used to cleanse crystals?
faq.a: Crystal tradition holds that selenite carries bright, clear energy that does not hold onto stagnant vibes, so stones placed on a selenite plate are said to be refreshed. It is a belief based on its pale, moonlike nature.
No. Selenite is a form of gypsum, which is soft and dissolves slowly in water. Water will dull the surface and can ruin wands. Keep it dry and wipe with a soft dry cloth.
Selenite is often considered self-cleansing, but you can refresh it with moonlight, sound, breath or a brief smoke pass. Avoid water, and keep it away from damp or humid rooms.
